1723 West Wabansia Avenue
Proposed Type 1 Zoning Amendment
Project Narrative

As a matter of background, Juliana Sung and Robert Gephardt own and currently reside within the
existing 2-story single.family home, located at 1723 West Wabansia Ave. (“Property”) along with
their family. The existing single family home was built in 2014. Juliana and Robert purchased the
Property in 2020, however have been long-time residents of the Bucktown neighborhood, since
2013. The Applicants are seeking to renovate and expand their existing “doghouse” located on
the roof of their existing single family home.

In order to proceed forward with their plans, the Applicants are seeking to amend the Property’s
existing RS3 zoning district to an RT3.5 zoning district, via a Type 1 zoning amendment
application. The Applicants are seeking the proposed expansion in order to continue to raise their
family in the Bucktown neighborhood. The Applicants have discussed their proposed plans with
its immediate neighbors, and have secured their support.

Please find an overview of the proposed Type 1 zoning amendment application.

1. Written description of request:

The Applicants are seeking to renovate and expand their existing “doghouse” located on the
roof of their 2-story single family home. The Applicants’ plan is to convert the existing storage
space and outdoor dining area, currently located on the roof, into fully enclosed space, or a
“penthouse” which will be accessible and utilized year round, rather than limited to access
solely during warmer months of the year. The proposed increase in square footage is 200 feet,
or .95 FAR, which is allowed in the proposed RT3.5 zoning district..

Based on review of Property’s current conditions, Applicant’s project architect, Present
Future Architects (“PFA”) confirmed that the existing height is 37’-4”, rather than 32’-4” as
calculated by the previous architect. In order to provide for easy ingress and egress onto the
deck and optimal clearance from the penthouse, Applicants are seeking a building height
increase from 37-4” to 38’-6” .

While the Chicago Zoning Ordinance allows for administrative relief for building height
(§17-3-1003-L), relief is not available for increase in FAR, unless the existing building has
been in existence for 50+years ( (§17-13-1101-G). For this reason, the Applicants must rezone
the Property, rather than strictly seek administrative relief. In this instance, Applicants’
administrative relief (10% increase in building height), is included as part of its proposed
Type 1 zoning amendment application, pursuant to Section 17-13-0303-D of the Chicago
Zoning Ordinance.
